capabilities: intercept: the attacker learns every message sent on the network (Dolev-Yao network control)
key_secrecy: knows_key(key) ⇒ given_key(key): keys are unforgeable (the crypto assumption)
replay: a known message can be re-injected into any session (sent in a new session)

decompose.detail_no_key: secret NOT derivable — decompose is gated by key knowledge (secrecy holds)
decompose.detail_with_key: attacker derives the plaintext secret by decomposing the intercepted ciphertext with the leaked key

replay.detail_base: replayed message accepted in a new session — no freshness binding
replay.detail_fixed: replay rejected — acceptance requires a session-fresh nonce the replay lacks

scope: Bounded relational Dolev-Yao adversary: composable capabilities (intercept / decompose / compose / key-secrecy / replay) over an explicit knows() relation. Derivability uses the sound entailment reading (knows(X) iff negation UNSAT). Demonstrates: (a) decompose leaks a secret ONLY when the key is known; (b) a cross-session replay is accepted without freshness and blocked with it, while a legitimate fresh message is still accepted. Bounded, not an unbounded proof.
